thread.title: Stock Market Goes On Wild Ride Down; Ciena, Adobe, Costco, Delta, Google| Investor's Business Daily

author: IBD STAFF
title: Stock Market Goes On Wild Ride Down; Ciena, Adobe, Costco, Delta, Google| Investor's Business Daily
text:
The stock market went on a wild ride, rallying early but ultimately closing lower. Global economic concerns worried investors, even as China cut tariffs on U.S.-made autos and reframed its Made in China 2025 tech ambitions, while Canada granted bail to Huawei's CFO. Ciena ( CIEN ) reported its best earnings growth in years, while Adobe ( ADBE ) and Delta Air Lines ( DAL ) gave weak earnings guidance. Costco Wholesale ( COST ) missed on earnings while Starbucks ( SBUX ) trimmed long-term growth forecasts. Google 's ( GOOGL ) CEO Sundar Pichai went before Congress, supporting privacy legislation and defending the search giant's practices.
X Stock Market Volatile The major stock market averages started the week off with gains but reversed lower. The S&P 500 index and Dow fell 1.2%, both hitting multi-month closing lows Friday. The Nasdaq composite slid 0.8%. China agreed to buy U.S. soybeans, end its 25% retaliatory tariff on U.S.-built autos and reframe its Made in China 2025 global tech ambitions to include broader market access for the U.S. and other countries. Ciena had stellar earnings growth. U.S. economic data were solid but China and Europe weakness grew. Adobe, Delta Air Lines and Starbucks gave weak earnings guidance.
U.S. Economic Data Solid The American consumer remains solid and inflation remains well contained, this week's two big economic reports showed. Retail sales rose a better-than-expected 0.2%, even as October sales growth was revised up to 1.1%. Core inflation, as measured by the consumer price index, rose 2.2% from a year ago in November.
But economic data in China and Europe continue to weaken. With the U.S. economy likely to decelerate in 2019 as tax-and-spending stimulus fade and U.S.-China trade concerns continue, it's unclear how many Fed rate hikes will occur after next week's expected move.
Ciena Earnings, Sales Growth Best In Years The maker of system-level optical products for communications networks and data centers reported adjusted fiscal first-quarter earnings were 53 cents a share, up 66%. Revenue rose 21% to $899.4 million. Those were the best EPS and sales gains in years. Ciena ( CIEN ) lifted its three-year revenue growth target slightly to 6%-8%. Analysts say Ciena has been gaining share versus Infinera ( INFN ). Ciena shares jumped to an 11-year high.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Adobe Earnings Guidance Light Digital media and marketing software giant Adobe ( ADBE ) topped Wall Street's targets for its fiscal fourth quarter, excluding its recent Marketo acquisition. But it came up short with its earnings guidance for the current quarter and fiscal year. Adobe shares fell 7.3% Friday.
Costco Earnings Miss, Stock Dives Costco ( COST ) stock plunged 8.6% Friday, breaching its 200-day line for the first time in over a year. For fiscal Q1, Costco earnings per share excluding items rose 18% to $1.61, missing estimates by a penny. Revenue including membership fees rose 10% to $35.07 billion, better than estimates for $34.63 billion. Comparable sales rose 8.8%, or 7.5% excluding gas prices, currency swings and an accounting change.
Google CEO Backs Privacy Legislation Sundar Pichai said at a House Judiciary Committee hearing that the internet giant supports federal privacy legislation to protect consumer data. The CEO of Google, the core unit of Alphabet ( GOOGL ), said the search giant gives its users "choice, transparency and control" on privacy. He told Republican lawmakers that Google's search engine isn't biased against conservatives. Google has "no plans" to relaunch a search engine in China though it is continuing to study the idea, he said.
Crude Oil Prices Fall As Traders Ponder OPEC Deal U.S. crude oil prices fell 2.7% to $51.20 a barrel as oil traders mulled the impact of the OPEC-Russia production cut amid slowing economic growth. The International Energy Agency said in a monthly report that OPEC created a floor for crude oil prices at its meeting last week, but it's unclear if the agreement will rebalance the oil market. In its own monthly report, OPEC said while its output fell in November, Saudi Arabia's production was near record levels. The cartel kept its 2019 oil demand forecast unchanged and lowered its non-OPEC 2019 production growth outlook. The Energy Information Administration reported a 1.2 million-barrel drop in U.S. oil stockpiles, less than the 2.6 million barrel drop analysts expected. ConocoPhillips ( COP ) will keep capital spending flat for 2019, while Hess ( HES ) plans to increase its spending.
Delta Air Lines Sees GDP Slowing Delta Air Lines ( DAL ) forecast 2019 revenue growth and profits below some analysts' forecasts. The carrier also said it expects continued fuel price volatility and a "slight deceleration in global GDP." Delta stock fell, and other airlines fell with it. Still, the carrier stressed that demand is strong. It also said it has a variety of tools — including its partnership with American Express ( AXP ) and more diverse sources of sales that rely less on main-cabin seats — to help manage swings in oil prices and a potential economic slowdown.
Tivity Health Buys Nutrisystem Tivity Health ( TVTY ) which provides fitness and health improvement programs, will acquire nutritional supplements and weight management form Nutrisystem ( NTRI ) for $1.4 billion in cash and stock. Tivity stock fell 34.5% to its lowest level since February 2017.
News In Brief Robinhood, the free stock-trading app, launched savings and checking accounts that will pay 3% interest, well above what even the highest-yielding online bank accounts offer. Robinhood says the accounts are insured by the SIPC, but the brokerage industry watchdog says maybe not
Caterpillar ( CAT ) said retail sales of its construction and mining equipment rose 16% from a year ago in the three months through November, slowing from 18% growth a month earlier and 25% growth as recently as June. Construction equipment was particularly weak in Asia.
Starbucks ( SBUX ) sees long-term non-GAAP earnings growth of at least 10%, down from prior forecasts for 12%. The coffee house giant also sees China same-store sales growth of 1%-3% over time. That overshadowed alliances with Alibaba ( BABA ), UberEats and more. Starbucks stock fell 2.35% Friday.
Gilead Sciences ( GILD ) tapped Roche Holdings executive Daniel O'Day to become its new CEO on March 1. O'Day has led the Swiss drug giant's pharmaceuticals unit since 2012.
American Eagle Outfitters ( AEO ) earnings rose 30% to 48 cents, beating by a penny. Revenue also beat, growing 5% to $1 billion. But shares of the youth-oriented clothing retailer fell on weak fourth-quarter guidance.
Pivotal Software ( PVTL ) reported a smaller-than-expected Q3 loss of 5 cents a share as revenue rose 30% to $168.1 million, also beating. Q4 guidance topped estimates.
Restaurant-arcade chain Dave & Buster's ( PLAY ) stock gapped down and hit its lowest level since June after same-store sales missed some estimates and 2019 revenue guidance came in light. Investors ignored a surprise Q3 earnings gain.
Apple ( AAPL ) plans to spend $1 billion to build a new campus in Austin, Texas. The iPhone maker also announced plans for new sites in Seattle, San Diego and Culver City, Calif. It also will expand in other U.S. cities including Pittsburgh, New York and Boulder, Colo., over the next three years.
After a five-year absence from the stock market, Dell Technologies plans to return to public trading on Dec. 28 under the ticker symbol DELL. The enterprise computing firm is doing a reverse merger with DVMT ( DVMT ), a tracking stock for Dell's ownership stake in VMware ( VMW ).
Tencent Music Entertainment ( TME ) raised $1.1 billion with an initial public offering that priced at 13, at the low end of expectations. Shares rose 8% in their debut but closed the week at 12.81. China's largest online music streaming service is a spin-off of China internet giant Tencent Holdings ( TCEHY ).
Stitch Fix ( SFIX ) reported quarterly results that topped expectations but the stock plunged on concerns that subscription growth of its online apparel services fell below expectations.
DSW ( DSW ), a shoe-store chain, reported third-quarter earnings that beat analyst estimates. The company also raised its full-year EPS outlook. Shares jumped, then sold off.
